subject: Recap & next steps — procurement route / AWS Marketplace interest
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@brightgrid.io>, Sophie Zhang <sophie.procurement@brightgrid.io>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps — procurement route / AWS Marketplace interest

Hi Alex and Sophie,

Thanks again for the discovery today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on procurement path and commercial mechanics: 

What we heard
- BrightGrid wants to proceed with Redwood for inference (primary use: customer-facing summarization service).
- Preference toward marketplace billing (AWS Marketplace) but procurement may require a standard PO rather than card.
- Key must-haves: SOC 2 report, SSO/SAML, invoices/PO processing timeline, and confirmation of how committed pricing / discounts are handled on marketplace listings.

Open questions for procurement team
- Does procurement need Redwood to issue a standard Redmond/DoC-style purchase order (PO) to your AP team, or do you prefer an AWS Marketplace Private Offer where AWS invoices on your behalf?
- Is there a minimum contract term required to issue a PO?
- Legal: any non-standard contract redlines we should flag now?

Attachments I’m including:
- Redwood_SaaS_AWS_Marketplace_FAQ.pdf (quick marketplace billing options)
- SOC2_TypeII_2024.pdf (control report)
- SOW_template_redwood.docx (example SOW we can adapt)

Proposed next steps
1) Sophie — can you confirm preferred billing route (PO to Redwood vs AWS Marketplace private offer) and internal PO timeline?
2) If PO is preferred, please share AP contact and any PO template. If marketplace is preferred, confirm whether you want a private offer.
3) We can have a short procurement sync next week (15–20 min) — are you available Tue/Wed afternoon PST?

Happy to loop legal/finance on our side — cc’d Dylan and Rishi.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0119

From: Alex Mercer <alex@brightgrid.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Zhang <sophie.procurement@brightgrid.io>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 17:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — procurement route / AWS Marketplace interest

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap.

Quick answers from our side: we definitely want marketplace billing if possible because our cloud budget runs through AWS, and that simplifies chargebacks. Procurement, however, is insistent on a PO being issued for anything over $50k. So two options they suggested:

1) AWS Marketplace Private Offer where AWS handles billing but we still create a PO that references the private offer (preferred by procurement).
2) Direct PO to Redwood (we can do this, but it requires some additional SOW paperwork and will go through our AP workflow which takes 2–3 weeks).

Other notes:
- Timeline: ideally we close commercial terms this quarter (by 2025-11-30) if possible.
- Security: SOC2 doc looks good; we also need an attestation of encryption-in-transit and confirmation on SSO provider support (we use Okta).
- Pricing: we'd like clarity on whether committed annual spend can be reflected as a discounted private offer, or if pricing on the public marketplace listing is the only option.

Thanks — Sophie (procurement) will coordinate the PO details.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 18:10:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — procurement route / AWS Marketplace interest

Marissa — good thread. Short answers and proposed internal owner/next steps from our side: 

Marketplace vs PO: Redwood supports AWS Marketplace SaaS Private Offers and can accept PO flow tied to a private offer. That allows BrightGrid to keep cloud spend aligned while still issuing a PO for AP. We can also accept a direct PO to Redwood if they prefer — both are supported.

Pricing/Private Offers: we can create a private offer with committed pricing / term and apply discounts tied to an annual commitment. Private offers are the mechanism many customers use when procurement wants a PO + committed pricing.

Security/Docs: attached SOC2 report is the right doc to share; Dylan can confirm SSO/Okta integration details (SAML metadata exchange steps).

Operational asks:
- Neha — can you prepare a draft private-offer packet (pricing + terms) and the billing flow notes we can send to Alex/Sophie?
- Dylan — can you prepare a short SSO checklist and expected timeline for onboarding?
- Marissa — I suggest we propose a 20-min procurement sync (AP + procurement + Neha) and send a stub private offer by end of week.

I’ll loop legal if BrightGrid raises any redlines beyond our standard SaaS terms.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

- Draft AWS Marketplace Private Offer packet (Neha) — includes committed pricing options and billing flow notes.
